info.title: AnswerThePublic Public API
info.description:
> **This API is in Alpha.** It is under active development. Endpoints,
> response shapes, rate limits, and plan eligibility can change without
> notice, and `v1` does not yet carry a stability guarantee or a
> deprecation window. Build clients that ignore unknown fields, and check
> this page before depending on any behaviour in production. The stage
> that applies to your workspace is reported by `GET /me` as
> `api_version`.

The AnswerThePublic Public API lets you run keyword research programmatically
and pull the same data the in-app dashboard shows — questions, prepositions,
comparisons, and alphabeticals — across the providers AnswerThePublic
supports (Google Web, YouTube, Bing, Amazon, TikTok, Instagram, ChatGPT,
Gemini).

Use it to integrate keyword discovery into your own tooling: content
pipelines, dashboards, briefs, internal portals, or automated workflows.
Searches you create through the API are stored in your workspace exactly
like searches run from the UI, so the two surfaces stay in sync.

Two resources do most of the work: **searches** (the keyword queries
you create — they cost search credits) and **reports** (the structured
output of a completed search — read-only, and free of search credits,
though fetching one spends the daily read allowance described under
**Rate limits**). Each is explained in detail in its own section below.

## Quick start
1. Open **Account → API Access** in your AnswerThePublic dashboard and
   enable API access for the workspace.
2. Create a Personal Access Token, choose its scopes (see below), and copy
   the token — it is only shown once.
3. Call `GET /api/public/v1/me` with the token in the `Authorization`
   header to confirm the workspace and scopes.
4. Create your first search with `POST /api/public/v1/searches`.

## Authentication
Every endpoint requires a Personal Access Token issued from the
AnswerThePublic account settings. Tokens are prefixed with
`atp_pk_live_` and are sent as a Bearer token in the `Authorization`
header:

```
Authorization: Bearer atp_pk_live_<your-token>
```

Tokens are tied to a single user **and** a single workspace, and they
inherit that user's role and that workspace's plan. Treat them like
passwords — never check them into source control or share them between
workspaces. You can revoke a token at any time from the same settings
page; revocation takes effect immediately.

## Scopes
Scopes are chosen when the token is created and cannot be changed later.
A request that uses a scope the token does not hold returns `403 Forbidden`
with a message naming the missing scope.

| Scope             | Grants                                                                      |
|-------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `searches:read`   | List and retrieve searches and their snapshots                              |
| `searches:write`  | Create new searches (consumes plan credits)                                 |
| `reports:read`    | Retrieve report payloads — keywords, volumes, intents, sentiments, sources  |
| `ai:read`         | List AI prompts on ChatGPT/Gemini reports (first call per report generates them and consumes plan credits) and poll generated AI answers |
| `ai:write`        | Request AI answer generation (consumes plan credits)                        |

Pick the **minimum** set of scopes a given integration needs. A read-only
dashboard, for example, never needs `searches:write`.

## Workspaces
AnswerThePublic groups searches, members, and billing under a **workspace**.
A token is bound to one workspace at creation time, and every endpoint
operates implicitly on that workspace — you never have to pass a workspace
ID. To create searches in a different workspace, mint a separate token
inside that workspace.

Call `GET /api/public/v1/me` to discover which workspace, plan, and
scopes the active token resolves to. This is also the cheapest call to
use as a health check.

## Plan eligibility
The API requires an **active, fully paid, recurring** AnswerThePublic
subscription — that is, a Monthly or Annual plan. Four plan and billing
states are blocked, each with its own `403` and its own machine-readable
`error_code` (see **Errors** below). They are not the only causes of a
`403`: the workspace opt-in toggle and the workspace lock are covered
further down.

| Workspace state | `error_code` | Message |
|-----------------|--------------|---------|
| No active paid plan — free, canceled, or paused | `ineligible_plan` | `Plan does not support API access` |
| **Lifetime plan** | `lifetime_api_access` | `API access is available on Monthly and Annual plans. Upgrade your plan to use the API.` |
| Trial not yet converted to a paid subscription | `trial_api_access` | `API access is available once your trial converts to a paid subscription` |
| Unpaid invoice — the subscription is in dunning | `unpaid_invoice` | `API access is paused until your outstanding invoice is paid` |

**Lifetime plans do not include API or MCP access.** Lifetime is a paid
plan, but it is a one-time purchase rather than a recurring subscription.
API and MCP access require a Monthly or Annual plan.

**Treat `atp_tier` as a label, not as the rule.** It is not what decides
access, and the two can disagree in both directions. A paid tier is not
sufficient: an unconverted Business trial already reports `atp_tier: t3`,
and a workspace in dunning keeps reporting the tier it bought. A
`lifetime` label is not conclusive either: a workspace that follows the
upgrade path above briefly holds both subscriptions, and eligibility is
decided from the subscription records with the recurring plan winning, so
it can legitimately get a `200` while still reporting `lifetime`. Call
`GET /me` and treat the `200` itself as the answer.

The workspace's tier is reported by `GET /me` as `workspace.atp_tier`:

| `atp_tier`   | Plan                           | API access | What it means                                                                                                    |
|--------------|--------------------------------|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `t1`         | Starter / Individual           | Yes        | Entry-level recurring paid plan. Lowest monthly search allowance.                                                |
| `t2`         | Growth / Pro                   | Yes        | Mid-tier plan with a larger monthly search allowance and more concurrent users per workspace.                     |
| `t3`         | Business / Expert / Enterprise | Yes        | Highest-tier plans. Largest search allowances, full provider coverage, and priority for enterprise integrations.  |
| `restart`    | Restart                        | Yes        | Legacy reactivation plan, billed monthly or annually, so it is a recurring subscription and eligible. Read `quota.searches` from `GET /me` for its allowance rather than assuming. |
| `lifetime`   | Lifetime                       | **No**     | One-time purchase plan. API and MCP access are not included — upgrade to a Monthly or Annual plan to use them.    |

Each `POST /api/public/v1/searches` consumes credits from the workspace's
search allowance, just like a search created from the UI. That allowance is
per billing cycle on current paid plans, and per day on free plans and on
grandfathered pre-v5 paid plans — so paid does **not** imply per-cycle. Read
`quota.searches.period` from `GET /me` rather than assuming. Hitting it
returns `429`, usually with `resets_at` and a `Retry-After` header; upgrade
the plan or wait for the next period to resume.

## Workspace opt-in
Even with a valid paid plan, a workspace owner must explicitly turn on
API access from **Account → API Access**. Until then, every request from
the workspace's tokens returns `403 API access is disabled for this
workspace`. Toggling the flag off invalidates every token minted for the
workspace immediately — useful as a kill switch if a token leaks.

## Workspace lock
A workspace can also be temporarily **locked** by AnswerThePublic — for
example after an overdue invoice, a payment failure, or a billing dispute.
While the workspace is locked, **every** public-API endpoint returns
`403 Workspace is locked. Please contact support or complete your
subscription.` until the lock is cleared. The lock is enforced
namespace-wide so reads and writes both stop together — there is no
"read-only locked" state to design around.

## Rate limits
Two kinds of ceiling return `429 Too Many Requests` — a short-lived
**request rate** and a per-period **allowance**. When a
`Retry-After` header is present it gives the number of **seconds** to wait:
back off until it elapses, then retry. The per-minute throttle always sends
it; the quota ceilings send it whenever the reset instant is known (see
below). Treat a 429 without it as "retry later on your own backoff".

**Request rate — several per-minute ceilings, all short-lived** (the
`Retry-After` is on the order of a minute):

| Scope | Default |
|-------|---------|
| Per token | 60 / min |
| Per workspace (all its tokens combined) | 240 / min |
| Per IP address | 300 / min |
| Per token on the AI endpoints (`/reports/{id}/ai/*`) | 10 / min |

Splitting a workload across several tokens raises the per-token ceiling but
not the per-workspace one, so 240/min is the effective cap for a single
workspace. The AI ceiling is deliberately much stricter than the general one.
For sustained higher throughput, contact support.

**Search quota — your plan's keyword-search allowance.** `POST /searches`
returns 429 once the allowance for the current period is spent. Here
`Retry-After` can be hours or days, and `error.details` tells you exactly
where you stand. `Retry-After` and `resets_at` are **omitted** when the
reset instant cannot be determined reliably; treat that as "retry later on
your own backoff", not "retry now":

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "Search limit reached",
    "code": 429,
    "details": {
      "quota": 200, "used": 200, "remaining": 0, "period": "cycle",
      "resets_at": "2026-08-01T00:00:00Z", "retry_after": 129600
    }
  }
}
```

When `resets_at` is present, do not retry before it — the answer will not
change. The monthly AI **answer** allowance behaves the same way
(`Answer limit reached`, with its own `resets_at`). The AI **prompt**
allowance does not fail at all: prompts beyond it come back `blank: true`
inside a 200.

**Read quota — a daily allowance on the read endpoints.** `GET /searches`,
`GET /searches/{id}` and `GET /reports/{id}` share a per-day allowance,
reported as `quota.reads` on `GET /me`. Exhausting it returns 429 with
`error_code: "read_quota_exceeded"`, `period: "day"` and a `resets_at` at
the coming UTC midnight, so the wait is hours at most:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "Daily read limit reached",
    "code": 429,
    "error_code": "read_quota_exceeded",
    "details": {
      "quota": 2000, "used": 2000, "remaining": 0, "period": "day",
      "resets_at": "2026-09-01T00:00:00Z", "retry_after": 37800
    }
  }
}
```

The AI read endpoints share it too. `POST /reports/{id}/ai/prompts` re-serves
stored prompts on repeat calls, so it spends the allowance whenever it
returns content, and is refused once the allowance is gone — unless the call
is generating the prompts for the first time, which is never refused.
`POST /reports/{id}/ai/answer` spends the allowance when it returns a
completed answer but is **never refused** for it: an answer is retrievable
exactly once (`task_id` is required, and completing an answer clears it, so a
repeat call returns `404`), and refusing would strand work your monthly
AI-answer allowance already paid for. `POST
/reports/{id}/ai/answer_request` spends nothing, because it commissions new
work against that same monthly allowance.

**A read only spends the allowance when it actually returns results.**
Polling `GET /searches/{id}` while a search is still running is free, however
often you do it, and so is any 4xx, 5xx or failed search, an empty listing, a
page that comes back with no rows on it, and a filter combination that
matches nothing. `GET /me` is never counted at all, so you can poll it to
check where you stand without spending anything.

`POST /searches` spends the allowance too, but only when it answers with
finished results inlined, which is what a repeat call for a keyword you
already searched in the last 24 hours does. It is never refused for the read
allowance: once you are over it, a create still succeeds but stops inlining
results, returning the async `status` shape instead. Fetch the data from
`GET /searches/{id}` or `GET /reports/{id}` once the allowance resets.

`per_page` is capped at **500** on every read endpoint. A larger value is
clamped rather than rejected.

To stay ahead of either quota rather than discovering it on a rejection, read
the `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset`
(seconds until reset) headers on the response, or poll `GET /me`, whose
`quota.searches` and `quota.reads` blocks carry the same numbers. Unlimited
plans omit the `RateLimit-*` headers entirely, and `RateLimit-Reset` is
omitted on its own when the reset instant is not known.

`RateLimit-*` always describes **the allowance governing that endpoint**: the
search allowance on `POST /searches`, the daily read allowance on the four
gated actions. They are separate budgets, so do not compare the numbers
across endpoints.

Note that `RateLimit-*` never describes the per-minute request rate:
`RateLimit-Remaining: 88` does not license an 88-request burst, and the
per-minute throttle's own 429 carries only `Retry-After`.

This API is intended for server-to-server use and is not callable from a
browser page: the CORS origin allow-list covers only AnswerThePublic's own
frontends, so a cross-origin request from your own site is rejected before it
reaches the API. Keep your token server-side regardless.

A `403` is never fixed by an immediate retry — see the table below.

## Errors
Every error response carries an `error` object with a `message` and the
numeric `code`. Two further fields are optional, and **no response carries
both**: `error_code` on the plan and billing rejections, `details` where
extra structured context exists.

The plainest form is message plus code, which is what a missing scope
returns:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "Token is missing required scope: searches:write",
    "code": 403
  }
}
```

A plan or billing rejection adds `error_code`:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "API access is available on Monthly and Annual plans. Upgrade your plan to use the API.",
    "code": 403,
    "error_code": "lifetime_api_access"
  }
}
```

A validation failure adds `details`, mapping each rejected field to its
messages, with `message` repeating the first of them:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "can't be blank",
    "code": 422,
    "details": { "keyword": ["can't be blank"] }
  }
}
```

`code` repeats the numeric HTTP status. `details` also carries the quota
breakdown on a 429 (see **Rate limits** above); it is absent everywhere
else, including on the missing-scope 403, which names the scope in
`message` only.

`error_code` is a **stable, machine-readable** label for the specific
cause, present only on the four rejections below. `message` is always
English and its wording can change, so branch on `error_code` rather than
on `message`.

| `error_code` | Status | Cause | Clears when |
|--------------|--------|-------|-------------|
| `ineligible_plan` | `403` | The workspace has no active paid plan — free, canceled, or paused. | A Monthly or Annual plan is purchased or reactivated. |
| `lifetime_api_access` | `403` | The workspace is on a Lifetime plan, which does not include API or MCP access. | The workspace upgrades to a Monthly or Annual plan. |
| `trial_api_access` | `403` | The subscription is still in its trial. | The trial converts to a paid subscription. Access follows within minutes, and within six hours at worst. |
| `unpaid_invoice` | `403` | The payment processor holds an unpaid invoice for the subscription. | The invoice is paid. Access restores on its own, normally within minutes of the payment clearing and within six hours at worst. |

Other errors — a missing scope, a `404`, a validation `422` — carry no
`error_code` and are described by `code` and `message` alone. Common status
codes you should plan for:

| Status | When you'll see it                                                                                                 |
|--------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `401`  | The `Authorization` header is missing, malformed, or the token is revoked, expired, or belongs to a deleted user. |
| `403`  | Token is valid but the request is blocked by policy: missing scope, the workspace's plan does not include API access (see **Plan eligibility**), the workspace opt-in toggle is off, or the workspace is locked. Retrying the same request changes nothing — fix the cause. The two billing causes (`trial_api_access`, `unpaid_invoice`) lift on their own once the billing state changes. |
| `404`  | The resource (search, report) does not exist or belongs to a different workspace.                                  |
| `422`  | The request body failed validation. `error.details` lists the offending fields.                                    |
| `429`  | **Recoverable**: per-minute request rate exceeded, or your plan's search / AI / daily-read allowance is spent. Honour `Retry-After` when present; otherwise back off on your own schedule. `error_code` is `read_quota_exceeded` for the daily read allowance and absent for the others. |
| `5xx`  | Transient server error. Retry with exponential backoff; if it persists, contact support.                            |

## Versioning
All endpoints are namespaced under `/api/public/v1`. Breaking changes
are intended to land under a new prefix (`/v2`, etc.), but **while the
API is in alpha that is an intention rather than a guarantee**: `v1`
carries no committed deprecation window yet, and the notice at the top of
this page is the operative statement. Additive changes — new optional
fields, new endpoints, new providers — can land in `v1` without notice, so
build clients that ignore unknown fields.

tags.name: Me
tags.description:
Inspect the user, workspace, plan, and scopes the active token resolves
to. Useful as a health check, for surfacing the workspace name in your
own UI, and for confirming a token's scopes before issuing a write call.

tags.name: Searches
tags.description:
A **search** is one keyword query against one provider, scoped to one
language and one region. For example, `marketing automation` in
English / United States on Google Web is one search; the same keyword
on YouTube is a separate search.

Creating a search via `POST /api/public/v1/searches` actually creates
a **parent search** that fans out into one search per provider you
selected (or every provider, if you didn't pick one). Each provider's
search runs its own asynchronous pipeline — autocomplete suggestions,
AI prompts where applicable, and cost-per-click enrichment — and
stores the result as a **snapshot**.

Searches are the queryable unit: you can list them, filter them by
provider / language / region, and re-fetch a single one to check
whether its snapshot is ready. Running the same
keyword + language + region twice in the workspace inside a 24-hour
window reuses the existing search instead of consuming credits again.

tags.name: Reports
tags.description:
A **report** is the structured output of a completed search — the
keyword rows you would see on the AnswerThePublic dashboard,
complete with monthly search volume, cost-per-click, intent and
sentiment labels (where the provider supports them), and source
breakdowns (questions, prepositions, comparisons, alphabeticals,
related).

A search produces a report; a report belongs to a search. Reports
are read-only and cost no search credits, but a fetch that returns
rows spends one of your daily reads (see **Rate limits**) — call
`GET /api/public/v1/reports/{id}` to slice the
same data different ways using the query parameters (filter by
provider, narrow by source bucket or category, sort, range-clip
volumes, etc.).

The mental model: **searches cost credits to create; reports cost no
further credits to read.** Run the search once, then surface its
report everywhere (dashboard, briefs, internal tools) without
spending another search credit.

Reading is not unlimited, though. A fetch that returns rows spends
one of the workspace's daily reads, and is refused once that
allowance is gone — see **Rate limits**. The two budgets are
separate: search credits meter what you CREATE, the daily read
allowance meters what we SERVE.

tags.name: AI
tags.description:
AI endpoints surface the prompts and generated answers tied to
ChatGPT and Gemini reports. A **prompt** is a question we have
pre-built or your team has written for a given report; an
**answer** is the generated text returned by the underlying AI
provider.

The flow is split into two phases so you can keep an HTTP request
cheap while the model runs:

1. `POST /reports/{id}/ai/answer_request` enqueues a generation job
   and returns a `task_id`. Answer either a pre-built prompt
   (`ai_prompt_id`) or your own free-form `question` grounded in the
   report's data — supply exactly one. This call consumes plan credits
   and requires `ai:write`.
2. `POST /reports/{id}/ai/answer` polls the same `task_id` until
   the underlying model finishes. While `status` is `processing`
   the body has no `ai_answer` and the call spends nothing; once it
   flips to `completed` the answer is inlined and that call spends
   one daily read. It never consumes plan credits, and it is never
   refused for the daily read allowance — it is the only way to
   collect an answer your monthly allowance already paid for.
   Uses `ai:read`.

`POST /reports/{id}/ai/prompts` returns the prompts tied to a
report. It is `POST` rather than `GET` because the **first** call
against a report generates the prompts on demand, which consumes
plan credits the same way a ChatGPT or Gemini search does.
Subsequent calls return the existing prompts from storage and cost
no further plan credits, but each one that returns prompts spends a
daily read, and those repeat calls ARE refused once the allowance is
gone. The first, generating call is not. Uses `ai:read`.

ReadQuotaExceeded.description:
Either the per-minute request rate was exceeded, or the workspace's
DAILY read allowance is spent (`error_code: read_quota_exceeded`, with
`quota`, `used`, `remaining`, `period: "day"` and a `resets_at` at the
coming midnight UTC in `error.details`). Only reads that actually return
results count toward the allowance — polling a search that is not ready
is free, and so is `GET /me`. Honour `Retry-After`.

**Free does not mean exempt.** Once the allowance is spent these
endpoints are refused outright, so a poll that would not have been
charged is refused too, and an in-flight search is unobservable until the
allowance resets. `POST /searches` is never refused, so a client can
start work it cannot then watch. `GET /me` keeps answering throughout.

RateLimit-Limit.description: The daily read allowance. Absent on unlimited plans and when the 429 came from the per-minute throttle.

RateLimit-Remaining.description: Reads left today. Absent in the same cases as `RateLimit-Limit`.

RateLimit-Reset.description: Seconds until the read allowance resets.

Error.description:
Standard error envelope. Every non-2xx response uses this shape so
clients can rely on a single error parser.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong. Safe to surface to end users, but always English — see `error_code` for anything your client needs to branch on.
message.example: Token is missing required scope: searches:write

code.description: HTTP status code, mirrored here for convenience when the error envelope is forwarded across a queue.

error_code.description:
Stable machine-readable cause, present only on the four plan
and billing rejections (see **Errors** in the introduction).
Absent on every other error, including the missing-scope 403.

details.description:
Optional map of structured context: `{"keyword": ["can't be blank"]}`
on a 422, or the quota breakdown on a 429. Absent everywhere
else, and never present alongside `error_code`.

Pagination.description:
Page metadata for list endpoints. Use `next` and `prev` to walk the
result set without computing offsets yourself; both are `null` at the
edges.

count.description: Total number of records that match the query, across every page.

page.description: 1-indexed page number this response belongs to.

pages.description: Total number of pages available given the current `limit`.

limit.description: Number of records requested per page.

from.description: 1-indexed position of the first record on this page within the full result set.

to.description: 1-indexed position of the last record on this page within the full result set.

prev.description: Page number to request to step backwards. `null` on the first page.

next.description: Page number to request to step forwards. `null` on the last page.

Search.description:
A provider-specific keyword search inside a workspace. Each ATP
keyword query produces one Search per provider — for example a
single `keyword + language + region` may fan out into separate
Search rows for `gweb`, `youtube`, `bing`, etc., grouped under one
`parent_search_id`.

id.description: Stable identifier for this provider-specific search. Use it with `GET /api/public/v1/searches/{id}`.

keyword.description: The query the user entered, normalised (trimmed, case-folded).

language.description: ISO 639-1 language code used for autocompletes (e.g. `en`, `es`, `pt`). Coerced to `en` for Instagram, which is English-only.

region.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 region code (e.g. `us`, `gb`, `de`). Coerced to `us` for TikTok and Instagram, which only honour the global feed.

provider.description:
Source the suggestions came from. One of:
`gweb` (Google Web), `youtube`, `bing`, `amazon`, `tiktok`,
`instagram`, `chatgpt`, `gemini`. Defaults to `gweb` when the
create call omits a provider.

slug.description: URL-friendly identifier for the search inside the AnswerThePublic dashboard.

workspace_id.description: Workspace that owns this search. Always equal to the token's bound workspace.

parent_search_id.description: Identifier of the parent search that groups every provider-specific run for the same `keyword + language + region`.

ParentSearch.description:
Aggregate row that groups every provider-specific Search produced by
a single create call. Returned by `POST /api/public/v1/searches` so
clients can track all providers' progress with one polling target.

parent_search_id.description: Identifier you can persist alongside the workspace to dedupe future create calls.

keyword.description: Normalised keyword shared by every child search.

language.description: Language shared by every child search (where the provider supports it).

region.description: Region shared by every child search (where the provider supports it).

workspace_id.description: Workspace that owns the parent search and all its children.

status.description:
Roll-up status across every child search. Use this single field to
decide whether to render results or keep polling.

- `pending` — the parent row exists but no provider snapshots have started yet. Rare; usually indicates an immediate failure to enqueue.
- `loading` — at least one provider snapshot is still being filled in the background. Poll again shortly.
- `completed` — every provider snapshot is fully populated and safe to read.
- `failed` — at least one provider snapshot exceeded the configured loading window without completing. Inspect the per-provider `searches[].status` to see which ones failed.

searches.description: One entry per provider that ran for this parent search. Use the per-entry `status` to render partial results as providers complete.

id.description: Use to fetch this provider's data with `GET /api/public/v1/searches/{id}`.

provider.description: Which provider this entry belongs to (`gweb`, `youtube`, `bing`, `amazon`, `tiktok`, `instagram`, `chatgpt`, `gemini`).

status.description: Status of this provider's snapshot in isolation, independent of the rolled-up `status` above.

snapshot.description:
Inlined snapshot payload. Omitted entirely when this provider is
still `loading` or has `failed` — poll
`GET /api/public/v1/searches/{id}` to fetch the data once it is
ready.

**Also omitted, with `status: "completed"`, when the workspace is
over its daily read allowance.** Inlining a finished snapshot is
a read, so once the allowance is spent the create still succeeds
but stops carrying results. Do not branch on
`status == "completed"` to decide whether `snapshot` is present:
check for the key itself. `quota.reads.remaining` on `GET /me`
tells you which case you are in, and the data stays reachable
from the read endpoints once the allowance resets at midnight
UTC.

Me.description: Snapshot of who the token belongs to and which workspace it operates in.

api_version.description:
Release stage label for the public API surface — one of
`alpha`, `beta`, `ga`. While in `alpha`, endpoints and rate
limits may change without notice. The label is sourced
server-side from a feature flag so it can be flipped
(`alpha` → `beta` → `ga`) without a client deploy.

user.description: The human who owns the token. Useful for audit trails in your own logs.

email.description: Email of the user who minted the token.

preferred_language.description: User's preferred locale for emails and the dashboard UI. Has no effect on API responses.

workspace.description: The workspace the token is bound to. Every endpoint operates on this workspace implicitly.

slug.description: URL-friendly workspace identifier — useful for deep-linking back into the AnswerThePublic dashboard.

name.description: Human-readable workspace name as set in workspace settings.

atp_tier.description:
Plan tier the workspace currently sits on. Maps to the
marketing names as follows: `t1` = Starter / Individual,
`t2` = Growth / Pro, `t3` = Business / Expert / Enterprise,
`lifetime` = Lifetime, `restart` = Restart (legacy
reactivation). **This is a label, not the access rule, and
the two can disagree.** A tier in this list does not imply
access: an unconverted trial or a subscription in dunning
keeps reporting the paid tier it bought while the API stays
blocked (`trial_api_access`, `unpaid_invoice`). Nor does
`lifetime` prove the opposite: eligibility is decided from the
subscription records, where a recurring paid plan wins, so a
workspace mid-upgrade from Lifetime to Monthly can report
`lifetime` here and still be served. Free workspaces cannot
reach this endpoint at all (`ineligible_plan`). See **Plan
eligibility** above.

token.description: The active token's metadata. The token value itself is never returned — store it when you create it.

name.description: Friendly label assigned at creation time, e.g. "CI pipeline" or "Reporting dashboard".

prefix.description: Non-secret prefix you can show in your own UI to help users identify which token is in use.

scopes.description: Scopes granted to the token at creation time.

last_used_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent successful request with this token. `null` if it has never been used.

expires_at.description: Optional hard expiry. `null` means the token is valid until revoked.

plan_slug.description:
Active paid plan slug (e.g. `business-month-4`), or `null` on free
plans. More specific than `workspace.atp_tier` — use it to map the
workspace to its exact plan.

links.description: Deep links back into the web app.

web.description: URL to this workspace's searches dashboard.

daily_search_budget_remaining.description:
Searches the workspace can still run today (mirrors the dashboard's
`search_left`). Same value as `quota.searches.remaining`, surfaced
flat for convenience before a `POST /searches` call.

quota.description:
What this token can do on the current plan. Current paid plans are
capped per BILLING CYCLE (t1/t2/t3 = 100/200/300; custom deals may
differ); free plans and grandfathered pre-v5 paid plans are capped
per DAY — read `searches.period` rather than inferring it from the
plan. AI answers and prompts are capped per MONTH. Poll this block to
self-throttle; it is the same source `POST /searches` enforces. The
`reads` block is the separate DAILY allowance on the read endpoints.

period.description:
`cycle` on current paid plans (billing-cycle window), `day` on
free plans and on grandfathered pre-v5 paid plans, whose
allowance was sold per day and clears at midnight UTC.

limit.description: Search allowance for the current period. Null means unlimited.

remaining.description: Searches still available in the current period. Null means unlimited.

resets_at.description:
When the allowance rolls over — the same instant a quota
`429` reports in `error.details.resets_at`. Null when
unlimited. Best-effort on subscription-anchored plans, where
it can be a day or two out; the 429 omits it rather than
reporting a value that has already passed.

reads.description:
Daily allowance shared across every metered endpoint and all
of the workspace's tokens: `GET /searches`,
`GET /searches/{id}`, `GET /reports/{id}`,
`POST /reports/{id}/ai/prompts`, `POST /reports/{id}/ai/answer`,
and `POST /searches` when it answers with results inlined. Only
spent by a call that actually returns results: polling a search
or an answer that is not ready yet is free, and so is
`GET /me` itself.

limit.description: Read allowance for today. Null means unlimited.

used.description: Reads that have returned results so far today.

remaining.description: Reads still available today. Null means unlimited.

resets_at.description:
The coming midnight UTC — the same instant a read-quota `429`
reports in `error.details.resets_at`. Null when unlimited.

limit.description: Max AI answers per month for the plan (e.g. t1=30, t2=300, t3=1000).
Max AI prompts per month for the plan.

get.summary: Retrieve token, user, and workspace context
get.description:
Resolves the active bearer token to the user, workspace, and scopes
it carries. Use this as:

- A **health check** before issuing more expensive write calls — if
  this returns 200, the token is valid and the workspace is API-eligible.
- A way to discover the workspace `slug` and `name` so your own UI
  can link back into the AnswerThePublic dashboard.
- A way to confirm scopes after rotating a token, without trying a
  write call and handling a 403.

Cheap to call; safe to hit on every cold start.

200.description: Token resolved successfully. Body contains the user, workspace, and token metadata.

401.description:
The `Authorization` header is missing, malformed, or the token
has been revoked, expired, or belongs to a deleted user.

403.description:
The token is valid but the workspace cannot use the API — either
the plan does not include API access, the workspace owner has
not enabled API access in settings, or the workspace is locked.

get.summary: List parent_searches in the token's workspace
get.description:
Returns a paginated list of `parent_search` rows in the token's
workspace, with each parent's per-provider child searches embedded.
A `parent_search` groups every provider-specific Search produced by a
single create call — listing parents instead of flat searches keeps
every provider for one keyword together in the response.

Use the query parameters to narrow the result set: filter by
`language`/`region` to compare across markets, by `provider` to find
parents that ran a specific provider, or pass `q` to find parents
whose keyword matches a substring. Pagination metadata in
`data.pagination` describes the parent_search list — `count` is the
number of parents, not the number of children.

**Required scope:** `searches:read`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-indexed page number to retrieve. Capped at 1000; a larger value is clamped, not rejected.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Number of `parent_search` rows per page. Larger pages reduce round-trips at the cost of a bigger response payload. Capped at 500; a larger value is clamped, not rejected.

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description: Order parents alphabetically by keyword (`asc` / `desc`). Default is most recently updated first.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: Restrict to parent_searches run in this region (e.g. `us`, `gb`, `de`).

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: Restrict to parent_searches run in this language (e.g. `en`, `es`, `pt`).

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description:
Restrict to parent_searches that have at least one child search of this provider
(`gweb`, `youtube`, `bing`, `amazon`, `tiktok`, `instagram`, `chatgpt`, `gemini`).
When this filter is applied, each parent's embedded `searches` array is also
narrowed to the matching provider — siblings from other providers are not returned.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Prefix-aware full-text filter on the parent_search `keyword` field — handy for finding "all parents mentioning automation".

200.description: List retrieved successfully. Empty `parent_searches` array if no records match the filters.

401.description: Token missing, malformed, revoked, or expired.

403.description: Token does not carry the `searches:read` scope, or the workspace cannot use the API (plan / kill switch).

post.description:
Runs keyword research against AnswerThePublic's providers and stores
the result in the workspace. The created `parent_search` groups the
per-provider Search rows so you can track all of them with one
identifier.

**Required scope:** `searches:write`.

## Cost
Each call consumes credits from the workspace's monthly allowance —
the same way a search created from the UI does. Hitting the
allowance returns `429` with `Retry-After` and a `resets_at`;
upgrade the plan or wait for the next billing cycle to resume
creating searches.

Reads (`GET /searches`, `GET /searches/{id}`, `GET /reports/{id}`)
cost no search credits, but they are not free: each one that
returns rows spends a daily read and is refused once that
allowance is gone. This endpoint spends a daily read too, whenever
it answers with results inlined, though it is never refused for
it. See **Rate limits**.

## Dedupe window
If a `parent_search` with the same `keyword + language + region`
was created in the workspace in the last 24 hours, it is **reused**
and **no additional credits are charged**. The response will return
the existing parent's id so your client can continue using the same
identifier idempotently.

## Async response — poll for completion
Keyword data is gathered in the background by per-provider jobs, so
the endpoint always returns `201` immediately. The response body
carries:

- `status`: rolled-up status across providers (`pending` /
  `loading` / `completed` / `failed`)
- `searches[]`: one entry per provider with its own `status` and an
  inlined `snapshot` *only* when that provider has already finished
  (e.g. a 24h dedupe hit reusing fully-populated data)

Poll `GET /api/public/v1/searches/{id}` per provider until its
`status` reaches `completed`, then read its snapshot. This pattern
never ties up an HTTP connection while jobs run, which matters
because a single search can take a long time across the slowest
providers + CPC enrichment.

## Provider selection
Without a `provider` field, the call fans out across every provider
AnswerThePublic supports (`gweb`, `youtube`, `bing`, `amazon`,
`tiktok`, `instagram`, `chatgpt`, `gemini`). Pass `provider` to
narrow the request to a single one — useful when polling rounds
cost something on your side.

keyword.description: The query to research. Whitespace is trimmed and case is folded server-side.

language.description: ISO 639-1 language code. Coerced to `en` for Instagram (English-only). Required so autocomplete locale matches your audience.

region.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 region code. Coerced to `us` for TikTok and Instagram, which only honour the global feed.

provider.description:
Optional. Restrict the call to a single provider —
one of `gweb`, `youtube`, `bing`, `amazon`, `tiktok`,
`instagram`, `chatgpt`, `gemini`. Omit (or pass
`null`) to fan out across every provider.

201.description:
Search created (or an existing one within the dedupe window was
reused). The body carries the parent search id and a per-provider
`searches` array; inspect each entry's `status` to know whether
its snapshot is ready.

RateLimit-Limit.description: Keyword-search allowance for the current period. Omitted on unlimited plans.

RateLimit-Remaining.description:
Searches left in the current period, counting the one just
created. Omitted on unlimited plans.

RateLimit-Reset.description:
Seconds until the allowance resets. Omitted on unlimited plans,
and when the reset instant cannot be determined.

401.description: Token missing, malformed, revoked, or expired.

403.description:
Permanently blocked — one of: token missing the `searches:write`
scope; workspace plan does not include API access; workspace API
kill switch is off; or the workspace is locked. `error.message`
distinguishes between them. Retrying will not help.

422.description:
Request body failed validation — typically a missing or empty
`keyword`, an unsupported `language`/`region`, or an unknown
`provider`. `error.details` lists offending fields by name.

429.description:
Recoverable, from one of two causes, distinguishable by the body:

- **Allowance spent** (`Search limit reached`): `error.details`
  carries `quota`, `used`, `remaining` and `period` (`day` or
  `cycle` — the window the allowance is measured over), plus
  `resets_at` and a `Retry-After` header when the reset instant is
  known — both are omitted otherwise, so branch on their presence.
- **Per-minute request rate exceeded**: no `error.details` at all and
  no `RateLimit-*` headers, just a message and `Retry-After`.

Retry-After.description:
Seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a per-minute
throttle rejection; on a spent allowance it is present only when
the reset instant is known.

RateLimit-Limit.description:
Keyword-search allowance for the current period. Present on a
spent-allowance rejection; absent when the 429 came from the
per-minute throttle instead.

RateLimit-Remaining.description:
Searches left in the current period (`0` on a spent allowance).
Absent when the 429 came from the per-minute throttle.

RateLimit-Reset.description:
Seconds until the allowance resets. Omitted when the reset
instant cannot be determined, and when the 429 came from the
per-minute throttle.

get.summary: Retrieve a single search and its latest snapshot
get.description:
Returns one provider-specific search and its most recent snapshot.
Use this endpoint to:

- **Poll for completion** after creating a search asynchronously —
  loop until `data.status` is `completed`, then read `data.snapshot`.
- **Re-fetch** an old search for a refreshed view of its snapshot.

The response always includes the search row, even when the snapshot
is still loading. Inspect `data.status`:

- `loading` — keyword pipeline (suggestions, AI prompts, CPC) is
  still running. Poll again shortly; one second between calls is
  plenty.
- `completed` — snapshot is fully populated. `data.snapshot` is
  safe to render.
- `failed` — the snapshot timed out. AnswerThePublic considers a
  snapshot failed if it has been loading longer than the configured
  ceiling (defaults to a few minutes). Re-create the search to
  retry.

**Required scope:** `searches:read`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Search identifier returned by `POST /api/public/v1/searches` (one per provider) or by `GET /api/public/v1/searches`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-indexed page number for this provider's suggestions. Capped at 1000; a larger value is clamped, not rejected.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Number of suggestions per page. Capped at 500; a larger value is clamped, not rejected.

200.description:
Search retrieved. Always includes the search row; the `snapshot`
field is populated only when `status` is `completed`.

snapshot.description: Inlined snapshot payload. `null` while the search is still loading or has failed.

status.description:
Status of the search's latest snapshot. Drives
whether `snapshot` is populated and tells the
client whether to poll again.

401.description: Token missing, malformed, revoked, or expired.

403.description: Token does not carry the `searches:read` scope, or the workspace cannot use the API (plan / kill switch).

404.description: No search with this id exists in the token's workspace. Either the id is wrong, or the search belongs to a different workspace.

get.summary: Retrieve report payload for a parent search
get.description:
Returns the structured report payload for a parent search — the same
data the AnswerThePublic dashboard renders as questions wheels,
prepositions, comparisons, alphabeticals, related, and source
breakdowns. The shape is the union of every provider's output;
unused fields are omitted on a per-provider basis.

Pass an `id` returned by `POST /api/public/v1/searches`
(the parent search id) or one of the per-provider ids — both work.
Use the query parameters to:

- **Filter** by provider, source, category, intent, or sentiment to
  drill into a slice of the data.
- **Sort** with `sort_by` + `sort_order` to surface highest-volume
  or lowest-cost keywords first.
- **Range** with `range_start_volume`/`range_end_volume` and
  `range_start_cost`/`range_end_cost` to clip outliers.
- **Paginate** with `page` and `per_page` for very wide reports.

This endpoint is read-only and does **not** consume search credits. It
does spend the daily read allowance whenever it returns rows: see
**Rate limits**.

**Required scope:** `reports:read`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Parent search id (or a per-provider search id) to fetch the report for.

parameters.name: providers
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of providers to include. Valid keys:
`gweb` (Google Web), `youtube`, `bing`, `amazon`, `tiktok`,
`instagram`, `chatgpt`, `gemini`. `google` is accepted as an
alias for `gweb`. Omit to include every provider. Unknown values
return `422` with the list of valid keys.

parameters.name: grouped
parameters.description: When `true`, results are grouped by category/source the same way the dashboard renders them. When `false`, returns a flat list.

parameters.name: source_name
parameters.description: Restrict to a single source bucket (e.g. `questions`, `prepositions`, `comparisons`, `alphabeticals`).

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Restrict to a single sub-category — typically the question word for `questions` source (`who`, `what`, `where`, `when`, `why`, `how`, `which`, `are`, `can`, `do`, `is`, `will`).

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-indexed page number for the keywords list. Capped at 1000; a larger value is clamped, not rejected.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Number of keywords per page. Defaults to 100; raise it to reduce round-trips on very large reports. Capped at 500; a larger value is clamped, not rejected.

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description: Field to sort by — typically `volume`, `cost_per_click`, or `keyword`.

parameters.name: sort_order
parameters.description: Direction for `sort_by`. Defaults to `desc` for numeric fields.

parameters.name: range_start_volume
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on monthly search volume. Use with `range_end_volume` to clip the keyword list.

parameters.name: range_end_volume
parameters.description: Inclusive upper bound on monthly search volume.

parameters.name: range_start_cost
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on cost-per-click.

parameters.name: range_end_cost
parameters.description: Inclusive upper bound on cost-per-click.

parameters.name: search_string
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring filter applied to the keyword text.

parameters.name: intents
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of intent labels to include — e.g. `informational,transactional`.

parameters.name: sentiments
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of sentiment labels to include — e.g. `positive,neutral`.

200.description:
Report retrieved. The `data` object's exact shape varies by
provider mix and `grouped` flag, but always carries the keyword
rows along with their volume, cost, intent, and sentiment fields
where the provider supports them.

data.description: Report payload — keyword rows plus the same metadata the dashboard renders. Shape mirrors the internal `/api/v1` reports endpoint.

401.description: Token missing, malformed, revoked, or expired.

403.description: Token does not carry the `reports:read` scope, or the workspace cannot use the API (plan / kill switch).

404.description: No parent search (or per-provider search) with this id exists in the token's workspace.

post.summary: Generate (or list) AI prompts for a report
post.description:
Returns the AI prompts attached to a single ChatGPT or Gemini
report, paginated. Prompts are the questions surfaced for the
report — both pre-built ones and any user-generated entries.

## Why `POST` for a "list" call
The first time this endpoint is hit for a report, the underlying
service **generates** the prompts on demand — they are not
pre-computed rows that already live in the database. Subsequent
calls return the same prompts from storage and behave like a
normal listing. We use `POST` so callers know the request is
non-idempotent and can mutate workspace data the first time
through.

## Credit consumption
Generating prompts consumes the workspace's plan allowance —
the same allowance ChatGPT / Gemini searches draw from. Going
over the monthly allowance does not fail the request: the extra
prompts are returned flagged `blank: true`, so check that flag
rather than expecting an error. They still carry their text and
still spend a daily read. Reads against an
already-populated report cost no further plan credits, but they do
spend a daily read and are refused once that allowance is gone.

**Required scope:** `ai:read`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
Any of three identifiers the workspace owns: a Report (snapshot) id, a
ParentSearch id, or a Search id. The endpoint resolves to the latest
chatgpt/gemini snapshot under whichever you supply. Same id you'd pass
to `GET /reports/{id}` works here — no need to learn a separate "snapshot
id" concept just for the AI subroutes.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-indexed page number to retrieve. Capped at 1000; a larger value is clamped, not rejected.

parameters.name: intents
parameters.description:
Optional comma-separated list of intent labels to include, e.g.
`informational,transactional`. Same format as the `intents` filter
on `GET /reports/{id}` — no array/repeated-param style is supported.

401.description: Token missing, malformed, revoked, or expired.

403.description:
Either the token does not carry `ai:read` or the workspace cannot
use the API (plan / kill switch). Retrying will not help.

404.description: Report id does not exist in the token's workspace.

429.description:
Per-minute request rate exceeded, or the daily read allowance is
spent (`error_code: read_quota_exceeded` — this endpoint re-serves
stored prompts, so it is metered as a read). Honour `Retry-After`.

The **first** call for a report is never refused this way: it
generates the prompts against your monthly AI allowance rather than
re-serving stored ones, so the daily read allowance cannot block it.
It still spends one read.
Note that exceeding the monthly prompt allowance does NOT fail: the
response stays 200 and the prompts beyond your allowance come back
flagged `blank: true`. They still carry their text, and any page that
returns rows spends a daily read.

post.summary: Request an AI answer for a prompt or free-form question (consumes credits)
post.description:
Enqueues a generation job and returns a `task_id` your client polls via
`POST /api/public/v1/reports/{id}/ai/answer`. This is the only
credit-consuming AI endpoint — every successful call charges the
workspace's plan allowance.

Supply **exactly one** of:
- `ai_prompt_id` — a canned prompt id from
  `POST /api/public/v1/reports/{id}/ai/prompts`, or
- `question` — a free-form question grounded in the report's data.

**Required scope:** `ai:write`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
Any of three identifiers the workspace owns: a Report (snapshot) id, a
ParentSearch id, or a Search id. The endpoint resolves to the latest
chatgpt/gemini snapshot under whichever you supply. Same id you'd pass
to `GET /reports/{id}` works here — no need to learn a separate "snapshot
id" concept just for the AI subroutes.

ai_prompt_id.description:
Identifier of a canned prompt the model should answer
(from `POST /api/public/v1/reports/{id}/ai/prompts`).

question.description:
A free-form question to answer using the report's data.
Use this instead of `ai_prompt_id` when the consumer wants
to ask their own question rather than a canned prompt.

200.description: Job enqueued. Hold the `task_id` and poll the answer endpoint.

401.description: Token missing, malformed, revoked, or expired.

403.description:
Either the token does not carry `ai:write` or the workspace cannot
use the API (plan / kill switch). Retrying will not help.

404.description: Report id does not exist in the token's workspace.

429.description:
Per-minute request rate exceeded, or the monthly AI answer
allowance is spent (message: `Answer limit reached`). When the reset
instant is known it is reported as `error.details.resets_at` plus a
`Retry-After` header; both are omitted otherwise.

Retry-After.description:
Seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a per-minute
throttle rejection; on a spent allowance it is present only when
the reset instant is known.

post.summary: Poll for an AI answer by task id
post.description:
Looks up the AI answer associated with the given `task_id`. While
the model is still working, the response carries `status: processing`
and no `ai_answer` payload. Once the underlying job finishes, the
same call returns `status: completed` with the inlined answer.

The `task_id` must belong to one of **this** report's prompts —
a `task_id` from a different report (whether in the same workspace
or another) returns `404`. Track the `task_id` you received from
`POST /reports/{id}/ai/answer_request` and always poll it against
the same report id you used to create it.

Does not consume search credits, but a completed answer spends the
daily read allowance (see **Rate limits**); polling a running task
does not. **Required scope:** `ai:read`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
Same id family as the prompts endpoint — Report (snapshot) id,
ParentSearch id, or Search id, all workspace-owned. Poll against the
exact id you used to call `answer_request`.

200.description: Either the polling status (`processing`) or the completed answer.

ai_answer.description: Present when `status` is `completed`. Shape mirrors `AiAnswerSerializer` from the internal API.

401.description: Token missing, malformed, revoked, or expired.

403.description: Token does not carry `ai:read`, or the workspace cannot use the API.

404.description:
The report id is not in the token's workspace, or the `task_id`
does not belong to one of *this* report's prompts (cross-report
task_ids are rejected, not redirected).

422.description:
`task_id` is missing or blank, or the underlying generation job
failed. `task_id` is required: without it there is no answer to
identify, and the request is rejected rather than resolved to an
arbitrary one.

429.description:
Per-minute request rate exceeded. Honour `Retry-After`.

This endpoint is **never** refused for the daily read allowance,
even when that allowance is spent: it is the only way to collect an
answer you have already paid for out of your monthly AI-answer
allowance, and nothing else retrieves it later. A completed answer
still spends one read, and polling a task that is still running
returns 200 with a bare `status` and spends nothing.
